name: Coinsbuy
rootCause: $8.07 million  lost from Coinsbuy across TRON and Ethereum in under an hour, then refilled ten drained wallets within half a day. One blog post since, no follow-up, Twitter account dormant since 2020. Nobody has said what actually failed.

descriptions.text: $8.07 million  lost from Coinsbuy across TRON and Ethereum in under an hour, then refilled ten drained wallets within half a day. One blog post since, no follow-up, Twitter account dormant since 2020. Nobody has said what actually failed.

Wallets linked to Coinsbuy (a B2B crypto payment processor) were drained of more than $7.9 million across Ethereum and TRON around 13:00 UTC on August 9, 2026. The attacker laundered part of the funds into Monero (XMR) via exchanges, while ChangeNOW helped freeze a six-figure amount; Coinsbuy temporarily paused deposits and withdrawals, which have since resumed.

On August 9, 2026, Coinsbuy, a centralized payments provider, suffered a cross-chain attack draining over $7.9 million from hot wallets on Ethereum and Tron. Attackers exploited privileged access, quickly laundering stolen assets through swap services and privacy networks. Coinsbuy replenished client funds from reserves, but the root cause remains undisclosed. The attack stemmed from unauthorized access to Coinsbuy's privileged wallet infrastructure, likely at the hot-wallet key management or admin controls layer. The exact technical breach (key compromise, admin session hijack, or internal control failure) has not been publicly confirmed or detailed by the company.
